lines.text: You sweat all the way up, then freeze at the top. Here's why.
Climbing in a warm jacket soaks your shirt.
On the summit, the wind hits that wet layer and pulls the heat right out of you.
The fix is layers. Start a little cool, and take the warm layer off before you climb.
Keep a fleece in your pack, and put it on the moment you stop.
Dry on the way up, warm at the top.
Save this before your next cold hike.
